name: Perfumes, attar and oud

problems.words: Oils sold by tola are measured by eye and the stock never balances
quick_ideas: Weigh your open oil bottles once and compare with recorded sales, because it shows how far off the measuring is
Start measuring loose sales instead of judging by eye, because small overpours add up.

workzap_build.text: oil stock in ml or tola per grade, deducted with each sale, with automatic variance checks and low-stock alerts per outlet.

problems.free_stops: the measuring routine and variance limits go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one busy day's oil poured with the tola sales written that day, so you see how much eye measuring drifts.
Give one person the job of writing every loose oil pour in one notebook, so stock checks match sales better.

problems.words: Expensive oud oil goes missing in small amounts
quick_ideas: Weigh your top-grade bottles at one shift change, because it tells you which shift the loss falls in
Limit who can open top grades, because fewer hands make gaps traceable.

workzap_build.text: a weigh-in at every shift change on phone for high-value oils, with variance flagged to the owner by outlet and shift.

problems.ask_first: How many people handle the top grades?
problems.free_stops: the control routine and access rules are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which role handled each top-grade bottle during one full day, so the loss pattern narrows to a part of the routine.
Keep all top-grade bottle handovers in one notebook at shift change, so missing amounts can be tied to a handover.

problems.words: Only the master blender knows the recipes, and the same blend smells different each batch
quick_ideas: Get your best-selling blend's ratio written down with the blender, because one recorded recipe is the start
Give each new batch a number, because it lets you trace a complaint.

workzap_build.text: a recipe book with ratios, batch number, maker and date, with access limited to people the owner chooses.

problems.ask_first: Is any recipe written down today?
problems.free_stops: how recipes are recorded, protected and linked to batches is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Smell the same blend from two recent batches side by side, so you can judge how wide the batch difference really is.
Give one person the batch notebook for recipe notes and blend labels, so every repeat batch follows the same written record.

problems.words: We run out of bottles, caps or boxes before Eid
quick_ideas: Count your packaging now and compare with what last Eid used, because the gap is your order
Ask suppliers their Ramadan lead time, because it sets your real order date.

workzap_build.text: packaging stock with reorder alerts timed to the season ahead, for every outlet.

problems.ask_first: How far ahead do you order packaging today?
problems.free_stops: reorder levels and seasonal timing go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare current bottles, caps and boxes on hand with last Eid's busiest days, so shortages are spotted before packing stalls.
Give one staff member the packaging count list and one fixed count time, so Eid prep stops relying on rough guesses.

problems.words: Kiosk cash doesn't match, and every kiosk reports on WhatsApp differently
quick_ideas: Agree one closing format for all kiosks, because mixed formats can't be compared
Check one kiosk's slips against its cash, because it shows whether the gap is general or local.

workzap_build.text: a kiosk close on phone sent automatically to the owner, cash matched to sales, and one morning read across all outlets.

problems.ask_first: How many kiosks or shops do you run?
problems.free_stops: the close-out fields and checks are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each kiosk's closing note against cash on the same evening once, so you see which reporting style hides the mismatch.
Give one person the job of collecting all kiosk closings in one place nightly, so differences are caught before the next day.

problems.words: Staff give away too many samples and decants
quick_ideas: Record samples given for one week, because it shows the real cost
Agree a daily sample allowance per kiosk, because it gives staff a clear limit.

workzap_build.text: a sample and decant log per staff member with monthly cost by outlet.

problems.free_stops: allowance rules and reporting go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many samples and decants each kiosk gives in one busy day, so giveaway habits by location become visible.
Give one staff member the sample notebook at each kiosk, so every free decant is noted in the same place.

problems.words: Corporate gift orders with custom boxes and names miss deadlines
quick_ideas: Put all open corporate orders on one list with delivery dates, because clashes become visible
Get written sign-off before production, because late changes cause most misses.

workzap_build.text: a gift and corporate order tracker with custom details, approval, stage and delivery date.

problems.ask_first: How do corporate orders reach you?
problems.free_stops: the order stages and approval flow are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many open gift orders are waiting on box details or name approvals, so the real source of deadline slips stands out.
Give one person the single notebook for all custom gift orders and promised dates, so every handover follows the same list.

problems.words: Mall kiosk rent is eating the profit and I don't know which kiosk pays
quick_ideas: Put each kiosk's sales, rent and staff cost side by side once, because it shows which carry the others
Talk to your accountant before any lease decision.

workzap_build.text: outlet comparison of sales against rent and staff cost per kiosk, updated monthly.

problems.ask_first: Are your kiosks in the same mall or different ones?
problems.free_stops: the comparison model is set up in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one week's sales notes between kiosks against each kiosk's rent and staff presence, so the weakest location stands out clearly.
Give one person the weekly kiosk comparison page in one notebook, so rent discussions use the same routine each week.

problems.words: Customers loved a scent and we can't tell them when it's back
quick_ideas: Start a "tell me when it's back" list, saving numbers only with permission
Note which scents people ask for most, because those drive restock orders.

workzap_build.text: a consented scent preference list with restock and festival messages sent automatically.

problems.ask_first: Which scents run out most often?
problems.free_stops: the messaging plan is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many times each scent is requested after it sells out this week, so restock choices match what customers actually ask for.
Give one staff member one notebook for sold-out scent requests at the counter, so return updates can be managed from one place.

problems.words: Wholesale buyers take goods on credit and pay late
quick_ideas: Total what each wholesale buyer owes and for how long, because it shows who to chase first
Agree credit limits before the season, because limits are easier set early.

workzap_build.text: a wholesale credit ledger with ageing and automatic WhatsApp reminders.

problems.ask_first: How many wholesale buyers take credit?
problems.free_stops: limits and reminder timing go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark which wholesale buyers paid later than promised on the last round, so your follow-up starts with the slowest payers.
Give one staff member the credit notebook and a fixed review time, so overdue buyer follow-up happens every trading week.

never_say: Help to sell clones as genuine branded perfume, or to make fake branded labels or boxes.
Whether "inspired" names or packaging are legal; say "check with a lawyer".
Any advice on ingredient safety, allergies or skin reactions; a serious reaction means emergency care.
Dangerous-goods advice for shipping or storing alcohol-based perfume; say "check with your courier or adviser".
Help bypassing customs on oud wood or oils.

sample_reply.person: I run six mall kiosks and every night I get sales on WhatsApp in different formats, some totals, some photos of slips. What can I do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is very fixable. 1. Agree one closing format for all kiosks, because mixed formats can't be compared. 2. Check one kiosk's slips against its cash, which shows whether the gap is general or local. Workzap can do this automatically for you: each kiosk closes on a phone, cash is matched to sales, and you get one morning summary across every outlet. Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
